scope: TOML/env-file/process-env/flag precedence, empty-value handling, path anchoring, legacy database compatibility (src/settings/load.ts, src/settings/paths.ts, src/settings/inspect.ts, src/cli/arguments.ts, src/cli.ts config wiring, src/config.ts legacy loader, docs/CONFIGURATION.md)

findings.title: An empty string in a TOML int/bool field is a hard config_invalid error instead of 'unset', and the sibling text kind disagrees
findings.evidence: kinds.int is z.union([z.number().int(), z.string().regex(/^-?\d+$/)]) and kinds.bool is z.union([z.boolean(), z.enum(["true","false"])]); both reject the empty string during documentSchema.safeParse (load.ts:513), before setValue (load.ts:656-667) can apply the empty-means-unset rule. kind 'text' uses bare z.string() and does treat '' as unset.
findings.reproduction: Config with '[server] port = ""' -> resolveServerSettings throws SettingsError code=config_invalid, message 'Invalid configuration file <path>: server.port: Invalid string: must match pattern /^-?\d+$/'. '[server] metrics_enabled = ""' -> config_invalid 'Invalid input'. '[server] allowed_hosts = ""' (text) resolves to the default successfully. Probe 1, reproduced.
findings.recommendation: Accept "" for int/bool (add z.literal("") to the unions and skip it in applyDocument) so the documented rule holds, or narrow docs/CONFIGURATION.md:51-52 to text settings. Trigger for an operator is a templated config such as port = "${PORT}" with the variable unset; the server then refuses to start instead of falling back to the default.

findings.title: Legacy default database path is relocated from ./data/swarmforge.sqlite to the XDG location with no runtime signal
findings.evidence: Legacy src/config.ts:77 defaults SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH to './data/swarmforge.sqlite'; resolveServerSettings (load.ts:835-841) now injects defaultDatabasePath() from src/settings/paths.ts:67-73 ($XDG_DATA_HOME/swarmforge/swarmforge.sqlite else ~/.local/share/...). The resulting provenance is only 'default', and renderStartup (src/serve-command.ts:151-160) prints host/port/metrics but never the database path. .gitignore:6 ignores data/, showing ./data was the working convention.
findings.reproduction: loadConfig(<minimal valid env>) -> SWARMFORGE_DB_PATH = ./data/swarmforge.sqlite. resolveServerSettings({env, cwd}) -> /tmp/probe-…/.local/share/swarmforge/swarmforge.sqlite, provenance = 'default'. Probe 2, reproduced. Consequence (code-evidenced, not run against a populated DB): an upgraded deployment opens a fresh empty SQLite file, all prior teams/workers/history appear lost, and the old file is orphaned with no startup warning.
findings.recommendation: If the DB path resolved to the default while ./data/swarmforge.sqlite exists relative to cwd, refuse startup or log a prominent warning naming both paths; at minimum render the resolved database path in the startup banner.

findings.title: --url "" is accepted then silently ignored, so status connects to a different endpoint
findings.evidence: value() (arguments.ts:48-53) rejects only a missing value, and arguments.ts:77 stores the empty string verbatim as overrides.SWARMFORGE_URL. applyEnvironment (src/settings/load.ts:701) then skips it via 'if (!value) continue', so the flag is neither honoured nor refused.
findings.reproduction: parseArguments(['status','--url','']) -> {"overrides":{"SWARMFORGE_URL":""}}. With a config declaring client.url = 'http://config.example/mcp', resolution yields url = http://config.example/mcp with provenance 'config:…' and no error. Probe 3, reproduced. Inconsistent with sibling flags: --config "" fails loudly with config_invalid 'Cannot read <cwd>: EISDIR'.
findings.recommendation: Reject an empty --url in the parser with UsageError (the parser is documented as total and pure), or normalise empty flag values identically across --url, --config and --env-file.

findings.title: server.api_token in a config file never reaches the client surface, so status 401s against a server that requires a token
findings.evidence: resolveClientSettings calls merged(prepared, clientFields, options), so only client.url/client.token are applied; server.api_token (load.ts:278-283) maps to the same target key SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN but belongs to controlFields. docs/CONFIGURATION.md:63 and :68 map both rows to 'SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN', implying one shared value.
findings.reproduction: Config with [server] api_token set -> client.value = {"url":"http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp"} (no token), client.provenance = {"url":"default","token":"default"}, redactedSettings(client).secrets = []; the same file yields server SWARMFORGE_API_TOKEN present = true. Probe 4, reproduced.
findings.recommendation: Disambiguate the 'Setting' column for client.token vs server.api_token in docs/CONFIGURATION.md, and/or have config show emit a hint when the server token is set but the client token is not.

findings.title: config path omits the config file's own env_file from the reported env_files list
findings.evidence: reportConfigPath maps only command.envFiles into env_files and never reads the selected document, contradicting its own comment at cli.ts:209-210 ('the environment files layered on it') and docs/CONFIGURATION.md:61.
findings.reproduction: Local CLI: swarmforge config path --config <dir>/cfg/config.toml --env-file <dir>/extra.env, where cfg/config.toml declares env_file = 'secrets.env' -> {"config_path":"…/cfg/config.toml","exists":true,"env_files":["…/extra.env"]}, exit 0; cfg/secrets.env is absent from the report.
findings.recommendation: Parse the selected config and prepend its anchored env_file to the reported env_files (redacted), so the layering report is complete.
